- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b810ddb6f1635fdf58a901aa082f5de015bb80c8` → `packageMentionDocs`.

```sh

git fetch origin 05a61f2d583d711fb37af9757688b88875ae5854 && git checkout 05a61f2d583d711fb37af9757688b88875ae5854
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b810ddb6f1635fdf58a901aa082f5de015bb80c8 4caf9e6eff43c3a75a9aa56243f4254daf457163 && git checkout -B drift-repro b810ddb6f1635fdf58a901aa082f5de015bb80c8 && git merge --no-ff 4caf9e6eff43c3a75a9aa56243f4254daf457163
```

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a

> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b810ddb6f1635fdf58a901aa082f5de015bb80c8` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4caf9e6eff43c3a75a9aa56243f4254daf457163`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #20387 (body; comments 5865067775 triage, 5874143143 claim, 5875171240 os-dev-report), PR #20486 (body, 3-file list, net diff against merge-base `8e0285918` of `origin/main`), #20335 (body and its 6 comments, incl. the precision-policy ruling 5861208644 and the ACCEPT 5864113534), PR #20372's changeset, and the check-runs on the head (read twice; the last read is at the end of ③). Read-only git and REST GETs only; nothing built, run or re-run. The head is a true merge: parents `36d7b2a80` (branch) and `8e0285918` (`origin/main`), and main carried no driver-sql change between the H1 base `75b216924` and that merge-base.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. Route (a) over (b): right, and (b)'s rejection is sound.** Route (b) as ruled moves only the rows path. SQLite's native `sum` over a REAL column is a double sum (`0.30000000000000004`), so under (b) SQLite's native face would stand alone on the pin itself, and changing SQLite's native face is outside (b). Checked, not taken on trust: SQLite 3.43+ uses Kahan-Babuska-Neumaier, but over TWO addends the compensated result equals the naive sum (the final `sum + c` adds the exact rounding error back to an already correctly-rounded `t`, which rounds to `t` again; the 0.1 + 0.2 case lands on a tie that ties-to-even resolves to `0.30000000000000004`, matching the card's measured SQLite answer). Route (a) holds on every dialect for the pin, so triage's stop valve ("neither (a) nor (b) holds on some dialect") is not tripped. The scaled-integer form of (b) would also have rested on `scale`, which 2 of the 70 fractional-family declarations in `examples/` carry (reproduced: app-todo `estimated_hours`, `actual_hours`).

**2. The operand `cast(cast(x as text) as double precision)` / `cast(cast(x as char) as double)`: right.** On `numeric` / `DECIMAL` it is identical to a plain cast by construction, not only by the 20,000/20,000 measurement: PostgreSQL implements `numeric` to `float8` as `numeric_out` then `float8in`, and MySQL implements `DECIMAL` to `DOUBLE` as decimal-to-string then `strtod`. On a pre-exact-decimal `real` / `FLOAT(8,2)` column the text is the same text the client hands `find()` (node-postgres parses float4 text; knex drives mysql2 through the text protocol), so the operand adds what `find()` reads (`0.1`), where a plain cast widens binary32 (`0.10000000149011612`); pinned by the binary32 case and ablation 2. Edge cases judged: exponent notation (PostgreSQL's `float4out` can emit `1.2345679e+06`; `float8in` and MySQL's string-to-double both accept it; no loss) — right; `NULL` (`cast(NULL)` is NULL, aggregates skip it, the #15546 empty-group fold is unchanged) — right; locale (`numeric_out`, `float4out` and MySQL DECIMAL-to-CHAR are locale-independent, always `.`) — right; a connection's `extra_float_digits` moves `find()`'s text and the operand's text together — right. One residual, not a defect: MySQL `DECIMAL` cannot hold `NaN`/`Infinity`, but PostgreSQL `numeric` can (`NaN`; `Infinity` since PG 14). The text round-trip preserves the value, but the answer's TYPE for that edge moves: before, the presenter left a `numeric` `'NaN'` string as written (its stated rule on `AGGREGATE_ANSWER_KIND`); now a `float8` `NaN` arrives as a JS `NaN` number (JSON `null` at REST). Reachable only through raw SQL, since the write door refuses non-finite numbers (`z.number().finite()`); unmeasured, no `reach:`, carrier none.

**3. `AGGREGATE_ACCUMULATION` and `fractionalNumericFields`: right on both checks.** "Fractional" is decided by declared type alone: `numericColumnFor(type).kind === 'exact'` (`number`, `currency`, `percent`, `slider`, `progress`, `summary`, all `numeric(65,30)` / `DECIMAL(65,30)`) plus the driver's `float` alias; `rating` is `{ kind: 'integer' }`; the `integer` / `int` aliases are in `NUMERIC_SCALAR_TYPES` (so in `numericFields`) but not fractional; `boolean` / `toggle` are in `booleanFields`. `scale` is not consulted, and that is right: the physical column is `numeric(65,30)` whatever `scale` says, and the write seam does not enforce it (`numeric-column-representation.ts` records that a no-`scale` field accepts `0.33333`), so a declared `scale` is not a storage guarantee. An undeclared or external column with no numeric or boolean declaration keeps the database's own arithmetic (`accumulatesInDouble` is false); an introspected `float` is fractional (double); an introspected `bigint` / `integer` takes `avg` in double and keeps `sum` exact. Both fills (declared and introspected) and the shard alias carry the registry. `sum` over an integer-valued column: `'double-over-fractional'` with the column not fractional falls to as-stored, so the exact total is rounded once by the presenter (pinned: `9007199254740994`, which ablation 3 turned to `9007199254740992`). `count` / `count_distinct` / `min` / `max` are `'as-stored'` (pinned), and SQLite is guarded by `this.isPostgres || this.isMysql` (every SQLite cell stayed green under ablation 1). The `Record` over `AggregationFunction` makes a new function fail `tsc` without an entry.

**4. Deviation 1 (`avg` over an integer-valued column): inside the claim's surface and the card's defect class; no widening card needed.** The card names the class as "native exact-decimal answer vs the double rows path, one query two answers under `having` `$eq`", for `sum` AND `avg`. MySQL's `avg(rating 1, 2, 2)` answering `1.6667` (a `DECIMAL` average at `div_precision_increment` 4) and PostgreSQL's `numeric` average of `11 / 9` answering `1.2222222222222222` against JS `1.2222222222222223` are that class, measured at the engine and REST doors at base (the `sa $eq 5 / 3` and `fa $eq 1 / 3` rows). Same function, same operand, same file, no other claim on it, same gate family; triage's "non-integer column" described the `sum` case, and an average over integers is a non-integer quotient. Declared in the PR body and the changeset, pinned by the `three` / `nine` groups, and ablation 1 turned exactly those red.

**5. The heirs: confirmed, no SQLite-family face changes answer.** `TursoDriver` overrides `aggregate` (`turso-driver.ts:2370`): its remote face compiles through `remoteTransport.aggregate` (`remote-transport.ts:1483`, its own compiler; no driver-turso file is in the diff), and its local face calls `super.aggregate`, where `accumulatesInDouble` is false because neither `isPostgres` nor `isMysql` holds for a libsql / better-sqlite3 client spelling (neither getter is overridden in either heir). `SqliteWasmDriver` overrides none of `aggregate`, `accumulatesInDouble` or `doubleAccumulationOperand`. `Type Check · workspace` (success) covers both heirs' consumption of the new `protected` members.

**6. Deviation 3 (the pin's location): the committed pin holds the triage pin's meaning.** `having` is evaluated by the engine over the value this door returns: `applyHaving` in `having-filter.ts` delegates to `@objectstack/formula`'s `matchesFilterCondition`, whose `looseEq` is strict `===` for non-Date values. The committed test pins, on each of the three native cells, (i) the answer equals the rows path's arithmetic over `find()`'s own rows (row-order `reduce` over `toNumber`), (ii) the literals `0.30000000000000004` / `0.15000000000000002`, so the oracle cannot drift, and (iii) the equality outcomes `== 0.3` false, `$in [0.3]` false, `== 0.1 + 0.2` true — the same number-to-number comparison `having` makes. That fixes `having`'s answer on all four faces for the pin. The PostgreSQL and MySQL cells run in CI: `ci.yml` "Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)" runs the whole driver-sql suite with both live URLs and `OS_EXPECT_LIVE_DIALECT_MATRIX=1`, and it is `success` on this head. Residual, pre-existing and recorded on #20372: the engine and REST `having` doors on live PostgreSQL / MySQL remain a local measurement, because no CI job provisions the REST test's live cells. Wording error, no effect on the pin: the PR body and the test docblock say `having-filter.ts` compares with `==`; the comparison is formula's `looseEq` (`===`), identical for numbers.

**7. The published answer change: see ②.**

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/driver-sql`: `patch`, `Clause-②: no` — right. Clause ② is "a new key on a published payload" (`check-changeset-no-major`'s level axis); this diff adds no key and no export. `AGGREGATE_ACCUMULATION` and `isFractionalNumericType` are module-private; `fractionalNumericFields`, `accumulatesInDouble` and `doubleAccumulationOperand` are `protected` — a subclass seam on the class's `.d.ts`, whose only subclasses are in-repo and in the same 69-member fixed group with driver-sql — not a consumer-callable surface. The answer's SHAPE (a JS number under the same keys) is unchanged; its VALUE moves in the last place on two dialects, toward the arithmetic the package already published under PR #20372's `patch`, and triage 5865067775 ruled route (a) admissible under that policy, so it is a bug fix under a ruling, not a policy change. No BREAKING banner is owed, so no ADR-0087 marker is owed, and none is carried; `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` (which carry `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-adr-0087-registration` and `check-empty-changeset`) are `success`. Observation, not a defect: PR #20372's changeset sentence "A total that fits keeps its exact value" is narrowed by this change, on PostgreSQL / MySQL, to integer totals and dyadic fractions (its own examples `500`, `30.75`, `0.375` still hold); this changeset states the new arithmetic, the `0.3` to `0.30000000000000004` example and the consumer note, which is the declaration owed.

Changeset sentences, each judged against the diff, the spec tables and the servers' documented behaviour: the defect statement and the four measured values are consistent with the card's own table and with MySQL's `div_precision_increment` default and PostgreSQL's `numeric` division scale — TRUE; "`avg` accumulates in double ... over every declared numeric or boolean column" — TRUE (`'double'` reads `numericFields` or `booleanFields`); the fractional list — TRUE (the six `exact` types plus `float`); "`sum` over an integer-valued column ... keeps the database's exact integer total, rounded once" — TRUE; "`count`, `count_distinct`, `min` and `max` are unchanged. SQLite is unchanged." — TRUE; "Each value added is the column's text parsed as a double: the value the SQL client hands `find()`" — TRUE; "For the exact-decimal columns this equals a plain cast" — TRUE (by construction, above); "MySQL's `CAST(... AS DOUBLE)` needs MySQL 8.0.17 or later" — TRUE; the route paragraph — TRUE; "Double sums are added in row order, one after another" — TRUE for a serial plan (see ③ for PostgreSQL's parallel aggregate); "SQLite 3.43 and later adds with compensated summation" — TRUE; "already true of SQLite's two paths before this change" — TRUE; "Two addends cannot differ" — TRUE (the proof in ① item 1); the consumer note — TRUE.

### ③ Boundary flags

**`open_questions[0]` (3+ fractional addends on SQLite's native face): a residual to route to triage on its own card; it does not make this landing premature.** Triage's stop valve reads "neither (a) nor (b) holds on some dialect" for the ruled pin, and (a) holds on all four faces for `0.1 + 0.2` (two addends are deterministic under every summation scheme). The 3+-addend shape is a different shape: SQLite-only, in the last place, pre-existing at base between SQLite's own two paths (naive rows path vs compensated native), out of either route's reach (no SQL spelling makes SQLite's `sum` naive or PostgreSQL / MySQL's compensated), and inside the loss the one-double policy declares. The dev's `out_of_scope_findings[0]` carries class (a) and a `reach:` measured at the engine and REST doors on SQLite at base and head, so it passes the filing gate ①: the seat files it bare; options A / B / C are triage's, and A is what this PR does today. This PR lands.

**Added by this review, same family, to fold into that card as a note:** the H2 sentence "added in scan order, one value after another" holds for a serial plan. PostgreSQL's `sum(float8)` is parallel-safe: a parallel aggregate adds worker-partial sums in a different order, so a large group of 3+ fractional addends can differ in the last place from the rows path's left fold on PostgreSQL too. Unreachable at the pin, inside the declared loss, not measured; not a separate finding.

**`out_of_scope_findings[1]` (service-analytics `NativeSQLStrategy`): answered, stays a noted carrier-none item.** The reading is confirmed: `native-sql-strategy.ts:49-50` emits raw `SUM(col)` / `AVG(col)`, and `plugin.ts:447-484` auto-bridges it through `engine.execute()`; a cube measure on PostgreSQL / MySQL still adds exact decimals. No door was measured, so there is no `reach:`, and under the filing gate it stays an acceptance note; the seat measures a door before filing, if it chooses to.

**Deviation 2** (text operand, not a plain cast): answered in ① item 2 — right, pinned. **Deviation 4** (draft opened after the final gate run): process only; the branch was pushed at each step, the body cites the measured head, and the head's own check-runs are the verdict. **Deviation 5** (two light typechecks outside `os-verify-lock`): read-only typechecks; every build and test ran under the lock; CI's four type-check lanes are the verdict, all `success`. **Deviation 6** (model-free `Co-authored-by` pair): AGENTS.md governs the repo's commit trailers and no model identifier lands on GitHub (#18060); `check:commit-card-trailers` passed on each push. Right.

**PR-body sentences:** TRUE, with three notes. (i) "`having-filter.ts` compares the value with `==`" is FALSE in letter — formula's `looseEq`, strict `===` — and identical in effect for numbers. (ii) "driver-sql source identical from `07f81ea19` to `4caf9e6ef`" is TRUE for `sql-driver.ts` (byte-identical) and imprecise for the tree: the new test file moved 12 lines between those heads (type-tightening of the `agg` helper and the `DriverQuery` literal; no assertion moved), and the head's own CI ran the final file. (iii) The local gate, suite and ablation counts are the dev's transcript and are not re-run here (read-only); the check-runs below are the verdict. The `Fixes #20387` line, `Clause-②: no`, the H1 base `75b216924`, the `9cdffbe36` exact-decimal landing, the "true merge of `origin/main` (`8e0285918`)" sentence, "2 of the 70 fractional-family declarations carry a `scale`", the CI job description for Temporal Conformance, the MySQL 8.0.17 floor against the `mysql:8.0` image, and the analytics acceptance note each reproduce.

**Check-runs on `4caf9e6eff43c3a75a9aa56243f4254daf457163`, final read 2026-09-28T17:46:03Z:** 33 runs — 29 `success`, 3 `skipped` (Console Pin Gate, Build Docs, Packed-tarball smoke: the rostered skips), 1 `in_progress` (Test Core 5/6), 0 red. Named gates: Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL) `success` (the new PostgreSQL / MySQL value pins ran live); Lint & Repo Gates `success`; Check Changeset `success`; Type Check · workspace `success`; TypeScript Type Check `success`; Governed Surface Queue Guard `success`; Build Core `success`; the three claim / single-writer / part-of gates `success`. The landing act reads Test Core (5/6) to completion; a red there re-owes this record.
